exact_quote: For convenience, ld, st, and cvt instructions permit source and destination data operands to be wider than the instruction-type size, so that narrow values may be loaded, stored, and converted using regular-width registers.
context_before: PDF page 135: section 9.4 Type Information for Instructions and Operands, Table 26 type checking rules.
context_after: PDF page 135-136: 'When a source operand has a size that exceeds the instruction-type size, the source data is truncated (chopped) to the appropriate number of bits specified by the instruction-type size.'; Table 27 note 'chop = keep only low bits that fit'; PDF page 136: 'When a destination operand has a size that exceeds the instruction-type size, the destination data is zero- or sign-extended to the size of the destination register.'
reason_for_inclusion: The only PDF truncation/chopping rule that uses overflow-adjacent language is scoped to ld, st, and cvt instructions and to source operands whose size exceeds the instruction-type size. For base add.u32 the operands carry the instruction-type size .u32, so this rule does not determine the result when the mathematical sum exceeds the unsigned 32-bit range. Recorded for BLOCK-1 traceability; it does not resolve BLOCK-1.
